summary: The Work Explorer's session rows gained a context menu, and both entries reach it through the vocabulary the parity test already guards rather than through hand-written `when` clauses. `SESSION_ACTIONS` is a second registry beside `ROW_ACTIONS` — separate because a session action's `when` reads the SESSION and all twelve existing entries read only the set, so widening `RowAction.when` would have made every set action's signature lie about what it reads — but it mints tokens through the same `actionToken`, lands in the same `viewItem =~ /;act-...;/` menus, and is held to the same forward and backward parity assertions. **Copy Run Prompt** copies the framework's documented trigger phrase verbatim from the existing `buildStartNextSessionPrompt`, and appears on exactly ONE row per set: the session that phrase actually resolves to. That is narrower than the step's literal 'gate on status' reading, and deliberately so — the phrase is set-scoped, so an entry on session 4 while session 3 is next would start a different session than the row it was copied from. The gate borrows `planLeftClickActivation` for its set-level half (the two surfaces cannot drift on what a runnable set is) and adds `nextRunnableSessionNumber`. **Open Session Artifacts** discovers files by convention (`^s<N>-`, case-insensitive, files only, sorted) so `s3-` cannot swallow `s30-`'s evidence and a new artifact shape needs no code change; one match opens directly, several open a QuickPick, none produces a message naming the session, the set and the convention. The entry is unconditional and the folder is read on the CLICK, never on the tree scan — hiding it would have cost a readdir per session row on the path Set 115's decision 4 protects. The Set 110 S2 ruling that no menu entry targets a session row was written so a future addition would be a decision rather than a leak; this session is that decision, and the assertion was NARROWED to bucket and step rows rather than deleted. Round 1 found a real Major I had asserted against and did not have: my fail-closed rule on an unrecognised session status was UNREACHABLE, because `normalizeLedgerSessions` drops an unreadable entry instead of passing it through, leaving a hole in the numbering that my walk stepped straight over and nominating the wrong session. The fix fails closed on a number gap as well, which is strictly wider than the unknown-status flag the finding proposed — it also catches the sibling drop paths (a non-integer, numeric-string or non-positive `number`) that produce an identical hole. Verification: discovery ISSUES_FOUND (1 Major), supplementary clean, remediation-review VERIFIED with the fix accepted and zero findings.

reason.specifics: Session 4 must NOT run as written — `step-ledger-findings.md` disqualifies it on three independent grounds and the spec's own heading says so. The next orchestrator's first job is therefore a decision, not an implementation: re-author session 4 after the findings' section 7 prerequisites, or drop it and ship sessions 1-3. That call needs the live context of what sessions 1-3 actually built and what the round-1 Major taught about corrupt ledgers reaching the row model, which is exactly this session's context. No blocker, no cost pressure, no capability gap; verification stays cross-provider regardless.
